input_signals.name: Levered External Financing Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capital spending that exceeds internally generated operating cash flow must be financed externally; when the firm is already highly levered, that incremental funding is expensive, dilutive or debt-overhang-constrained, so the investment destroys equity value.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing gap (capx minus oancf, scaled by assets) isolates investment that cannot be self-funded, which is exactly the margin where distress matters, while the leverage rank supplies the fragility conditioning. Firms with a large gap but low leverage retain debt capacity and should not be penalized, so the multiplicative form encodes the true interaction rather than two additive effects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( capx, oancf ), at ) ), rank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unsold Inventory Buildup Under Weak Profitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUB(GROWTH(invt, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ib, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Working-capital investment growing faster than sales signals demand shortfall; when the firm is also unprofitable, that stranded inventory forecasts markdowns, write-offs and liquidity drain rather than anticipated demand.
input_signals.reasoning: The inventory-minus-sales growth wedge is an investment measure that is ambiguous on its own (it can reflect optimistic restocking), so its return implication should flip with the firm's profitability state. Weighting by the rank of negative ROA makes the penalty grow continuously with fragility, avoiding the sparse zero-mass of a binary loss flag.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sub( growth( invt, 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( ib, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Distressed Equity Issuance Financing
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operations cannot service their liability stock and which simultaneously tap the equity market are funding investment from the most expensive external source; such issuance signals urgent balance-sheet strain and predicts low subsequent returns, whereas identical issuance by cash-generative firms is benign growth financing.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 winner showed the payoff lies in externally financed investment, but it only measured the gap implicitly; sstk names the actual financing instrument, and oancf/lt measures whether internal cash flow can cover the debt burden. The interaction isolates equity raised out of necessity from equity raised out of opportunity, which a stand-alone issuance signal cannot separate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( oancf, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Payroll Expansion Under Weak Profitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(emp, 1)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Headcount is a quasi-fixed, hard-to-reverse investment; growing the workforce while three-year average profitability is poor locks in operating leverage precisely when the firm can least absorb it, forecasting restructuring charges and weak returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This opens a labor-investment channel entirely distinct from the capex and working-capital channels already in the archive, and quasi-fixed labor costs are the classic amplifier of distress risk. The three-year moving average of ROA measures a persistent fragility state rather than a one-year earnings blip, so the conditioning variable is not simply momentum in earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( emp, 1 ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( ib, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Acquisitive Growth With Depleted Retained Earnings
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(aqc, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisitions made by firms with a history of accumulated losses (negative or thin retained earnings) are transformational gambles rather than incremental bolt-ons, and typically overpay, producing later goodwill impairment and equity underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: Inorganic investment is a distinct margin from organic capex and is where managerial empire-building is most severe, while retained earnings capture cumulative rather than current-period fragility. The pairing tests whether the distressed-investment penalty is stronger for external growth than for internal growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( aqc, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funding Coverage of Liabilities
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating cash flow comfortably exceeds their capital spending relative to the total liability stock are self-financing and face no rollover or dilution risk; this free-cash-flow-to-debt capacity is underpriced and should earn positive abnormal returns, giving the resilience side of the story a well-populated long leg.
input_signals.reasoning: The prior resilience attempts used additive rank composites whose long leg mixed unrelated firms; expressing discipline as a single continuous coverage ratio makes the long portfolio an economically homogeneous set of self-funders. Scaling the free-cash-flow surplus by liabilities rather than assets ties investment restraint directly to the debt burden it must service, which is the distress channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( sub( oancf, capx ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Three-Year Self-Funding Coverage
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(oancf, capx), 3), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained ability to cover capital spending out of operating cash flow, measured against the total liability stock, identifies firms whose investment policy is genuinely self-financing; cumulating three years removes lumpy project timing and isolates structural financial resilience, which is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: The one-year version is the archive's best joint performer (fmb +2.69, Sharpe 0.42) and the three-year cumulation of the mirror deficit measure raised the short-side alpha from -4.3% to -4.5%, so horizon extension helped the burn side and should also smooth the resilience side. This isolates a single design choice — measurement horizon of the funding identity — on the construct with the strongest evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( ts_sum( sub( oancf, capx ), 3 ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Deficit-Only Funding Shortfall
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, oancf), lt)), INDICATOR(SUB(capx, oancf), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: The distress-investment interaction is inherently one-sided: only firms whose capital spending actually exceeds internal cash flow must approach external markets, so the return penalty should be confined to the deficit region while surplus firms are undifferentiated.
input_signals.reasoning: Every prior version of this construct treated the surplus and deficit sides symmetrically, which mixes two economically different states into one linear slope and may explain why the FMB t-stats were weaker than the portfolio evidence. Switching the signal off for self-funders tests whether the penalty is a genuine financing-constraint kink rather than a monotone cash-flow effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( capx, oancf ), lt ) ), indicator( sub( capx, oancf ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Total Investment Self-Funding Including Working Capital
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1))), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: True investment includes the cash absorbed by inventory buildup, not just fixed capital; the firms that fail the self-funding test are often those whose working-capital investment silently drains cash, and adding it should sharpen identification of firms heading for external financing.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-0 inventory-versus-sales signal produced the archive's strongest FMB slope among the negative-sign family (-2.46), indicating working-capital investment carries independent information about distressed expansion. Folding it into the funding identity tests whether the two best-performing channels are additive within one economically coherent cash-flow measure rather than needing a multiplicative interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, delta( invt, 1 ) ) ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Liability-Financed Capital Spending
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(capx, at)), RANK(GROWTH(lt, 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Investment matters for distress only when it is accompanied by an actual expansion of claims: firms increasing capital expenditure while their total liabilities are growing are levering up to invest, which raises default risk and dilutes equity holders.
input_signals.reasoning: All prior conditioning used a static leverage or coverage *level*, which cannot distinguish a firm that is currently levering up from one that has been levered for a decade; the flow of liabilities is the financing act itself. This tests whether the mechanism is contemporaneous debt-financing behavior rather than a stock-of-debt state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( capx, at ) ), rank( growth( lt, 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Total Investment Self-Funding Including Acquisitions
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inorganic investment consumes the same internal cash as capital expenditure, and acquisitions made by firms without the cash flow to fund them are the most aggressive form of distressed expansion, so the funding identity should be measured on total cash used for investment.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding working-capital investment to the identity preserved the FMB slope and improved the alpha t-stat from 1.93 to 2.26, suggesting the identity strengthens as it becomes more complete; acquisitions are the remaining large omitted use of cash. This also revisits the aqc channel, which produced a solid FMB slope (-2.30) but no tradable spread when used as a standalone rank product, testing whether it works only inside the funding identity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Capex Penalty Gated On Cash-Flow Insolvency
input_signals.expression: MUL(NEG(RANK(RATIO(capx, at))), INDICATOR(NEG(oancf), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capital spending is not intrinsically bad news; it becomes bad news only when the firm cannot generate positive operating cash flow at all, so the investment signal should be switched on exclusively inside the cash-flow-insolvent group.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-3 truncation experiment gated on the sign of the funding gap and destroyed the portfolio evidence, but it truncated the *investment* variable rather than conditioning on the *distress state*, which is what the economic story actually specifies. Gating on negative operating cash flow makes the short leg an economically homogeneous set of cash-burning heavy investors while leaving everyone else neutral, a cleaner test of whether the interaction is a genuine regime effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( neg( rank( ratio( capx, at ) ) ), indicator( neg( oancf ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Rank-Balanced Funding and Liquidity Composite
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), RATIO(che, lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Financing resilience has two separately informative dimensions — the flow of cash left after all investment, and the stock of cash already held — and each should contribute equally to the ranking rather than being dominated by whichever has the fatter distributional tail.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding cash inside the ratio raised the alpha to +5.5% but crushed the FMB slope to +0.93, which is the signature of a skewed level term overwhelming the flow term in the linear cross-sectional regression. Ranking each channel before combining equalizes their influence and should retain the portfolio gain while restoring the cross-sectional slope, isolating a pure aggregation-form design choice.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), ratio( che, lt ) )

input_signals.name: Funding Gap Against Near-Term Claims
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, capx), lct))
input_signals.hypothesis: What determines whether an investment program forces distressed refinancing is not the total liability stock, most of which is long-dated, but the claims coming due within the year; free cash flow measured against current liabilities is the sharper solvency test.
input_signals.reasoning: Every version of the identity so far has been scaled by total liabilities, which mixes a thirty-year bond with a supplier payable, whereas the refinancing risk that the story requires is concentrated in the near-term bucket. This isolates the denominator's maturity horizon as the design choice and would tell us whether the effect is about solvency (lt) or liquidity (lct).
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( sub( oancf, capx ), lct ) )

input_signals.name: Internal Self-Sufficiency Net of Equity Raised
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, capx), sstk), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that appears to cover its investment only because it sold stock is not self-funding at all; subtracting equity issuance from the surplus separates genuine internal sufficiency from investment sustained by dilutive external capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Distressed equity issuance was independently informative in gen 1 (fmb -2.00, alpha -2.8%), and the funding identity is precisely where it should belong economically, as the financing source that plugs the gap. This tests whether the identity's power comes from investment exceeding cash flow per se, or from the external capital that must be raised as a consequence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, capx ), sstk ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Three-Buffer Financing Resilience
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Financial resilience against an investment program has three separable buffers — this year's cash flow surplus after all investment, the cash already banked, and the lifetime of retained profits — and firms strong on all three are the ones the market persistently underprices relative to their default risk.
input_signals.reasoning: The two-channel version is the archive leader, and retained earnings is the one classic Altman buffer never yet added to it in additive rank form; when tested against the flow leg alone it gave fmb +1.95, so it is informative but was previously asked to carry too much weight. If the three-channel version raises the t-alpha above 3.40 the buffers are complements; if it dilutes, we learn the cash stock already spans the accumulated-profit channel.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Funding Surplus With Near-Term Liquidity Cover
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), RATIO(che, lct))
input_signals.hypothesis: The liquidity buffer matters relative to the claims that actually come due soon, not to the entire liability stack, so measuring cash against current liabilities gives a sharper reading of whether a firm can keep investing without touching capital markets.
input_signals.reasoning: Scaling the funding gap by current liabilities delivered fmb +2.49 versus +2.69 for total liabilities with an identical Sharpe, indicating the near-term denominator is at least as informative, but it has never been applied to the *liquidity* leg where the maturity logic is strongest. This isolates one denominator choice inside the archive's best structure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), ratio( che, lct ) )

input_signals.name: All-Uses Funding Surplus With Cash Buffer
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(ADD(capx, aqc), DELTA(invt, 1))), lt), RATIO(che, lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash consumed by inventory buildup is investment in every economically meaningful sense, so the funding surplus should net out fixed capital, acquisitions and working-capital investment together before being compared to the liability stock.
input_signals.reasoning: Each prior completion of the uses-of-cash numerator improved the evidence — adding working capital lifted the t-alpha from 1.93 to 2.26 and adding acquisitions lifted the FMB slope to +3.08 — but the two completions have never been combined inside the winning rank-composite structure. This tests whether the identity's power scales with its economic completeness or saturates.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( add( capx, aqc ), delta( invt, 1 ) ) ), lt ), ratio( che, lt ) )

input_signals.name: Worst-Year Self-Funding Capacity
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(TS_MIN(SUB(oancf, capx), 3), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is financially resilient only if it could fund its investment out of internal cash flow even in its weakest recent year; the minimum over the last three years measures the trough of the funding state, which is what determines whether a covenant or refinancing event was ever triggered.
input_signals.reasoning: Averaging over three years (TS_SUM) diluted the one-year signal, and first differences carried nothing, which together suggest the informative feature is not the trend or the mean but the downside of the firm's own funding distribution. TS_MIN is the natural temporal analogue of the weakest-link logic and is the one time-series concept the archive has not tested on the winning construct.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( ts_min( sub( oancf, capx ), 3 ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Total External Capital Raised
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(sstk, at), GROWTH(lt, 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Rather than inferring the funding shortfall from the cash-flow identity, measure the financing actually obtained: firms simultaneously issuing equity and expanding their liabilities are dependent on external capital to sustain their investment programs and subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs individually produced significant FMB slopes (equity issuance -2.00, liability-financed capex -2.22) but neither produced a reliable negative alpha alone, and each captures only one side of the external financing decision. Pooling them in the rank-additive form that repaired the composite family tests whether the short side of the story is best expressed through observed financing rather than through the inferred cash gap.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sstk, at ), growth( lt, 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Runway-Augmented Buffer Composite
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(che, oancf), ADD(capx, lct)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Coverage of committed near-term outflows by available resources and the surplus-after-investment relative to the debt stock are two non-redundant readings of the same resilience concept — one a multiple, one a margin — and pooling them by rank with the retained-earnings reserve should capture both the portfolio separation of the former and the linear cross-sectional slope of the latter.
input_signals.reasoning: The runway ratio produced the archive's largest alpha (+6.1%, t 3.71) but no FMB slope because it is a skewed multiple, exactly the pathology that rank pooling fixed once before when cash was moved out of the ratio and into a ranked channel. This directly merges the best-alpha construct with the best-slope construct in the aggregation form that has repeatedly repaired this problem.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( add( che, oancf ), add( capx, lct ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Four-Buffer Resilience With Working Capital
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, lt), RATIO(wcap, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net working capital is a fourth, distinct financing reserve — receivables and inventory can be run down to fund operations without touching capital markets — so adding it to the flow surplus, cash stock and retained-earnings reserve should further separate firms that can sustain investment internally.
input_signals.reasoning: Each buffer added so far has raised the FMB slope (from +2.27 with two channels to +3.51 with three) while holding alpha near 5%, so the question is whether the buffer set has saturated or whether the working-capital reserve carries independent information. A null or diluting result would tell us the composite is complete and the final generations should refine weighting rather than add channels.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), sumrank( ratio( re, lt ), ratio( wcap, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Buffers With Current Profitability Reserve
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(ib, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What protects a firm from its investment program is its current earning power relative to its debt burden, not the historical accumulation of past profits; substituting current income for retained earnings tests whether the third buffer works through present debt-service capacity or through accumulated cushion.
input_signals.reasoning: Retained earnings and current income are highly correlated but economically distinct — one is a stock of past success that may be stale, the other a flow that determines whether interest can be paid this year. This isolates a single channel substitution inside the leading composite and identifies which fragility concept the third buffer is really proxying for.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( ib, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: All-Uses Three-Buffer Resilience
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(ADD(capx, aqc), DELTA(invt, 1))), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The flow leg should net out every cash use that constitutes investment — fixed capital, acquisitions and working-capital buildup — before being compared to liabilities, so the most complete uses-of-cash definition combined with the validated buffer channels should dominate.
input_signals.reasoning: The all-uses numerator delivered alpha +5.2% with t 3.14 in the two-channel composite, and the three-buffer structure independently delivered the best slope and Sharpe, but the two improvements have never been combined. This is the last untested completeness dimension of the leading construct and should either confirm additivity of the two gains or reveal that inventory changes add noise once acquisitions are already netted.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( add( capx, aqc ), delta( invt, 1 ) ) ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Internally Sourced Buffer Composite
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), sstk), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A surplus achieved only because the firm sold equity is not resilience; purging issuance from the flow leg leaves a measure of genuinely internal financing sufficiency, which should be the cleaner predictor of subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Netting issuance out of the simple identity preserved the slope (fmb +2.39) but has never been tested where it matters most, inside the composite whose long leg may currently be populated by cash-rich firms that raised that cash externally. If this improves the leader, the mechanism is internal self-sufficiency; if it weakens it, market access itself is part of the resilience being priced.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), sstk ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capital Program Relative To Liquid Reserves
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), che)), RATIO(re, lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: The most fragile expanders are firms whose annual investment program is large relative to the cash they actually hold and who have no accumulated earnings cushion behind it; such firms must return to capital markets within months to keep investing.
input_signals.reasoning: Every prior investment-intensity measure was scaled by assets or PP&E, which says nothing about financing capacity, whereas scaling the capital program by the cash reserve expresses it in units of survival time and is a functional form the archive has never tested. Pairing it with the retained-earnings reserve in additive rank form keeps both legs populated and gives a short leg of cash-poor, deficit-laden expanders that is economically homogeneous.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( neg( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), che ) ), ratio( re, lt ) )

input_signals.name: Earnings-Based Buffer Resilience
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Income before extraordinary items is an economically equivalent measure of the internal resources available to fund a capital program, so replacing operating cash flow with earnings should preserve the resilience mechanism while extending it to the large set of firm-years where cash-flow-statement data are unavailable.
input_signals.reasoning: Every leading signal is capped near 0.087 coverage because oancf is the binding constraint, while the one construct avoiding it reached 0.121 coverage with fmb +2.90; if the earnings-based flow leg retains the slope and alpha, we gain roughly forty percent more usable observations and a longer sample without changing the economics. A material deterioration would instead tell us that accrual-free cash generation, not accounting profit, is what the market misprices.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( ib, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Flow-Weighted Multi-Horizon Buffer Composite
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lct), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The funding-surplus channel carries more information than either stock buffer, so it should receive greater weight, and measuring it against both total and near-term claims captures solvency and rollover risk as separate readings of the same surplus.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has only tested equal-weight channel pooling, yet the flow leg alone delivered fmb +3.08 while each stock buffer alone delivered less, implying the equal-weight composite underweights the most informative channel. Entering the surplus twice with different denominators doubles its effective weight while simultaneously testing the maturity-horizon question that gave fmb +2.49 in isolation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lct ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net-Liquidity Buffer Resilience
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(che, dlc), lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash that is fully offset by debt maturing within the year is not a buffer at all; the true liquidity reserve backing an investment program is cash net of short-term borrowings, and netting them should remove firms that look liquid only because they have drawn credit lines.
input_signals.reasoning: The cash channel is what drives the composite's portfolio alpha, but gross cash misclassifies levered firms holding borrowed balances as resilient, precisely the firms the distress story says should be short. This is a targeted economic correction to the highest-alpha channel rather than another added buffer, which the four-buffer test showed to be unproductive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( sub( che, dlc ), lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Internal Sufficiency With Earning Power
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), sstk), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(ib, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The most reliable resilience portfolio combines a funding surplus that was not manufactured by selling equity with a cash reserve and demonstrated current earning power against the debt burden.
input_signals.reasoning: The two highest-Sharpe variants in the archive were issuance-netting (0.565) and the current-profitability buffer (0.465), and each addressed a different weakness of the leader — externally financed surpluses and stale accumulated cushions respectively. Combining them tests whether their Sharpe improvements are independent, which matters because the objective values reliability of the spread as much as its size.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), sstk ), lt ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( ib, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Smoothed-Surplus Buffer Resilience
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), 3), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Annual capital programs are lumpy, so a single year's surplus misclassifies firms in a heavy build year as fragile; averaging the surplus over three years measures the firm's normal self-funding capacity while the stock buffers remain contemporaneous.
input_signals.reasoning: The stock buffers are already persistent by construction, so the composite's turnover and noise come almost entirely from the lumpy flow leg, which is a plausible reason its Sharpe stops at 0.55. Smoothing only that channel is a precise design intervention, distinct from the earlier failed attempt that cumulated the flow while dropping the buffer channels entirely.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ma( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), 3 ), sumrank( ratio( che, lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Buffers With Capital Program Burn Multiple
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), che)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: How many years of investment the cash reserve can sustain is an investment-intensity measure expressed in survival time, and adding it explicitly ensures the composite ranks firms on the aggressiveness of their capital program relative to their resources, not merely on how much cash they hold.
input_signals.reasoning: The burn multiple standalone gave fmb +2.90 and t-alpha 3.00 on a much broader sample (coverage 0.121), and it is the only high-performing channel in which investment appears in the numerator rather than being subtracted from cash flow, so it is the least redundant addition available. It also replaces the gross-cash channel, which should reduce the composite's tilt toward simply cash-rich firms while preserving the liquidity information through the denominator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( neg( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), che ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Burn Multiple With Multi-Horizon Surplus
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), che)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lct), RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The funding surplus deserves double weight and should be read against both total and near-term claims, since solvency and rollover risk are distinct failure modes, while the burn multiple supplies the investment-intensity dimension and retained earnings the accumulated cushion.
input_signals.reasoning: Double-weighting the surplus across two horizons produced the best Sharpe among high-slope signals (0.560 with fmb 3.38) and the burn multiple produced the best composite alpha (+5.9%), and the two improvements act on different parts of the ranking. The risk is coverage dilution toward 0.076, which the accompanying proposals hedge against.

input_signals.name: Internally Sourced Burn And Buffer Composite
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), che)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), sstk), lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is resilient only if its investment is small relative to its own cash and its surplus was not manufactured by issuing equity; purging issuance from the flow leg while retaining the burn multiple should give the most stable spread of any specification.
input_signals.reasoning: Issuance netting produced the two highest Sharpes in the archive (0.565 and 0.544) by removing firms whose apparent surplus came from selling stock, and the burn multiple contributed the largest composite alpha; combining them targets the reliability dimension of the objective directly. If Sharpe rises above 0.57 while alpha stays near 5%, this is the best risk-adjusted version of the mechanism.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( neg( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), che ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), sstk ), lt ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Burn Multiple With Current Earning Power
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), che)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), RATIO(ib, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Whether a firm survives its capital program depends on present debt-service capacity rather than a possibly stale stock of past profits, so current income relative to liabilities is the more forward-looking third channel alongside the burn multiple and the funding surplus.
input_signals.reasoning: Substituting current income for retained earnings in the three-buffer composite preserved the slope (3.45) and improved the Sharpe (0.465), indicating the two cushions are close but not identical proxies; it has not yet been tested alongside the burn multiple, where the interpretation shifts from cushion to debt-service coverage. This resolves which fragility concept the third channel should encode in the final specification.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( neg( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), che ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( oancf, add( capx, aqc ) ), lt ), ratio( ib, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Broad-Sample Burn And Earnings Buffers
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), che)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, ADD(capx, aqc)), lt), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The same resilience mechanism should be measurable on the much larger set of firm-years without cash-flow-statement data by using accounting income as the internal funding source, giving a version of the signal that is robust across the full sample rather than the post-1987 cash-flow era.
input_signals.reasoning: The earnings-based flow leg raised coverage from 0.087 to 0.121 while retaining fmb +3.07 and t-alpha 2.81, and its main weakness was a low Sharpe (0.255) that the burn multiple — itself estimable on the broad sample — is well suited to repair since it adds a liquidity dimension the earnings leg lacks. A strong result here delivers a signal whose evidence does not depend on the shortest and most recent portion of the sample.
